findings.title: Historical >2GB FP16 failure and superseded ByteSize-threshold workaround
findings.observation: A >2GB fp32 ViT-Huge export failed during fp16 conversion because shape inference serialized the full ModelProto. Disabling shape inference for models at or above 90% of the protobuf limit made the same build complete and yielded genuine fp16.

falsified_on: usyd-community/vitpose-plus-huge@9f36d7aec1800d23e97f10c2e74393aee92aa53f @ fp16 @ CPUExecutionProvider @ winml-cli b7a7b893: current main succeeds through the EncodeError-only retry from PR #1176 without the ByteSize/90% heuristic; see vitpose-013

gotchas: Do not use the historical ByteSize/90% prediction workaround. Current `vitpose-013` attempts normal conversion and retries with shape inference disabled only after `EncodeError`.
findings.mechanism_notes: The same model failed without and completed with disable_shape_infer; genuine fp16 was verified by dtype and size.
findings.symptom: winml build ... -p fp16 fails at the FP16 stage with google.protobuf.message.EncodeError: Failed to serialize proto (src/winml/modelkit/quant/fp16.py). Occurs for ViT-Huge and any model whose fp32 export exceeds ~2 GB.
findings.root_cause: ORT's convert_float_to_float16 runs ONNX shape inference by default. Shape inference serializes the full ModelProto, which exceeds protobuf's hard 2 GB single-message limit for large models.
findings.fix: SUPERSEDED by `vitpose-013`: attempt normal conversion, catch only `google.protobuf.message.EncodeError`, and retry with `disable_shape_infer=True`. Preserve the serialization root cause, not the ByteSize/90% heuristic.
findings.gate2_proof: Same model crashes with EncodeError WITHOUT the fix, and completes (FP16 stage 71.4s, Build complete 661.9s) WITH the fix. Genuine delta.

findings.title: SynthPose Base exports a traced 52-heatmap classic-decoder ViTPose graph
findings.observation: At checkpoint revision e1f00dc65c23aedd629089ba44b46154e84a7778, stanfordmimi/synthpose-vitpose-base-hf resolves to model_type=vitpose, task=keypoint-detection, class=VitPoseForPoseEstimation. The 90,003,508-parameter model has a 16x16 patch projection over 256x192 RGB crops, 12 encoder blocks at width 768 with 12 heads and 3072-wide MLPs, then ConvTranspose 768->256 and 256->256 plus a 1x1 Conv producing 52 heatmaps [1,52,64,48]. HTP metadata from WinML 0.2.0 recorded 197 total modules, 78 traced modules, 156 execution steps, input pixel_values torch.float32[1,3,256,192], and the backbone/encoder-layer/attention/MLP/classic-decoder hierarchy.

not_yet_tested_on: other SynthPose or non-Base ViTPose checkpoints

gotchas: This checkpoint has 52 outputs rather than the 17-output COCO contract recorded for vitpose-002.
HTP modules_traced/total_modules is 78/197; it is execution-trace coverage, not a claim that every registered PyTorch submodule emitted a distinct ONNX region.
findings.mechanism_notes: Pinned config, source-derived architecture probe, HTP hierarchy metadata, and ONNX I/O/topology agree on the class, dimensions, 12-block backbone, classic decoder, and 52-channel output.

findings.title: SynthPose Base CPU fp16 conversion is genuine half precision
findings.observation: Revised tester verdict 302526d6eafbfe39536cf139aa74e000c1532019d257b974ac3e6844339ca496 rebuilt model SHA-256 ac730176eb54c90f9ef87080e5dbeea798b3905489a7bdab75a3221299482912 for fp16 and 8b492bf731c8ad36900a010f25b68b917e042cbad7102f49a2e44fe76513290c for fp32. The CPU fp16 artifact retained float32 I/O but converted all 90,004,536 floating initializer elements to FLOAT16 with zero FLOAT initializer elements. Its final external data was 180,004,864 bytes versus 360,017,920 bytes for fp32 (ratio 0.4999886228); initializer names/dimensions and non-Cast topology matched fp32, with exactly two expected I/O Cast nodes.
gotchas: Use explicit --precision fp16 and do not suppress the quant/conversion stage; a recipe label alone is not proof of fp16.
findings.mechanism_notes: ONNX initializer dtypes, element counts, topology, Cast count, and external-data size independently confirm true fp16.

findings.title: SynthPose Base fp16 is slower than fp32 on the tested CPU runtime
findings.observation: Using the same VitPoseImageProcessor-derived person crop, 10 warmups, 100 measured iterations, and memory capture on CPUExecutionProvider/onnxruntime 1.24.5, fp32 measured mean 89.421 ms, p50 88.241 ms, 11.18 samples/s, and 379.29 MB total RSS delta; fp16 measured mean 118.169 ms, p50 117.193 ms, 8.46 samples/s, and 391.53 MB total RSS delta.
gotchas: Smaller fp16 storage does not imply lower CPU latency or memory for this runtime and host.
findings.mechanism_notes: The measured regression is reproducible evidence for this host/runtime only; no kernel-level cause was isolated.

findings.title: COCO-17 defaults cannot honestly evaluate SynthPose's 52-keypoint output
findings.observation: Exact fp32 and fp16 winml eval attempts were CLI-BLOCKED: the default local coco_keypoints_val2017 dataset was absent, and obtaining it would not make the metric valid because the model emits 52 keypoints while KeypointAPMetric defaults to 17 COCO names/sigmas and fail-closes on prediction/reference/sigma count mismatch. The checkpoint provides 52 names but no pinned compatible 52-keypoint annotation dataset/revision and no defensible 52-element OKS sigma vector.

not_yet_tested_on: a pinned SynthPose-compatible 52-keypoint dataset with justified OKS sigmas

gotchas: Never report COCO-17 OKS-AP for this 52-output checkpoint.

Diligence audit: prior vitpose knowledge was re-read; PR #905/#949/#1023 behavior was mined; explicit --task config and exact eval were attempted; EP options, narrower export ranges, and a custom inference harness cannot supply missing ground truth or justify OKS sigmas.
feature_gaps_filed: Evaluation unblocker: provide a pinned 52-keypoint annotation dataset/revision plus defensible 52-value OKS sigmas and keypoint_names; no issue/PR was filed by this learner run.
findings.mechanism_notes: Source inspection and PR mining confirm custom layouts are supported only when matching sigmas and keypoint_names are supplied. The remaining blocker is missing evaluation data/metric semantics, not model inference.

findings.title: SynthPose Base static analysis is complete across 11 EP/device rule targets
findings.observation: Revised tester verdict 302526d6eafbfe39536cf139aa74e000c1532019d257b974ac3e6844339ca496 refreshed analysis for model SHA-256 8b492bf731c8ad36900a010f25b68b917e042cbad7102f49a2e44fe76513290c (fp32) and ac730176eb54c90f9ef87080e5dbeea798b3905489a7bdab75a3221299482912 (fp16). Public rules v0.2.0 (SHA-256 6dcabbe7f5493fbc2bd23de195ab6e35b3578d510f18c2e220bc5538a1f232cc) produced 11/11 complete metadata/classification results at both precisions: CPU/CPU; CUDA/GPU; DML/GPU; MIGraphX/GPU; NvTensorRTRTX/GPU; OpenVINO/CPU, GPU, NPU; QNN/GPU, NPU; and VitisAI/NPU. Component mapping covered 423/423 fp32 and 425/425 fp16 nodes with zero unmapped. fp32 had 423 ops/13 types and fp16 425 ops/14 types; the top counts were Add=110, MatMul=96, and a third-place tie Reshape=50/Transpose=50 (both precisions), with fp16 adding Cast=2. findings.title: SynthPose Base recipes require the processor-normalized high-exclusive pixel range
findings.observation: Revised charter a821637da64f498d69088406d6ebaab68b15c119cd070a704223ed3f437e7a69 corrected Effort/Goal/Outcome to L2/L2/L2. Pinned VitPoseImageProcessor metadata derives the float32 graph-input domain [-2.1179039478302,2.640000104904175], represented high-exclusively as [-2.1179039478302,2.640000343322754); the semantic crop observed min=-2.1179039478302 and max=2.5702831745147705, falsifying [0,1) as the graph-input domain. Both recipes now persist the corrected range: fp32 recipe SHA-256 a00c2ca430726e08fd1c4a00db661cbb4c275e9375b6319aab89d06a95a2db0d and fp16 afb53b4b0f73cab80d6ec741c0b3bb1f15f0b69af8ea0969b499b0e359da7f85.
gotchas: Optimum's generated [0,1) image dummy range is not necessarily the post-processor graph-input domain; derive normalized bounds from pinned processor metadata.
The persisted range is canonical high-exclusive; np.nextafter(max_valid_float32,+inf) supplies the upper bound.
findings.mechanism_notes: The bounds were derived from pinned rescale/normalize metadata, checked against the semantic crop, persisted byte-for-byte in both build configs, and validated against both revised artifacts.

findings.title: Generic perf honors persisted high-exclusive input_value_ranges without model special cases
findings.observation: The generalized generate_random_inputs fix forwards every persisted io_config.input_value_ranges entry without model-id/model-type branching, preserves float low-inclusive/high-exclusive bounds, adapts integer high-exclusive bounds to the legacy inclusive NumPy generator, and retains [0,1) only for unspecified floats. Revised verdict 302526d6eafbfe39536cf139aa74e000c1532019d257b974ac3e6844339ca496 proved default fp32/fp16 VitPose generation stayed inside [-2.1179039478302,2.640000343322754) and emitted both negative and positive values. Negative sentinel [-9,-8), singleton integer [7,8), unspecified-float fallback, and co-located winml_build_config/WinMLSession persistence regressions passed; the full relevant tester gate reported 363 passed, 6 skipped, 1 xfailed plus passing changed-file Ruff, recipe pre-commit, and diff-scope checks.
gotchas: Integer high-exclusive ranges require subtracting one only at the legacy inclusive NumPy-generator boundary.
The implementation must stay model-agnostic; no VitPose/model-id branch is needed.
Methodology coverage already exists in _meta-017, which identified generic perf dropping recipe value_range and requested this durable propagation fix; do not append a duplicate _meta finding.
findings.mechanism_notes: Unit-level range cases, persisted build-config integration, per-artifact generated-range proofs, and 100-iteration default perf independently exercised the same generalized path.

findings.title: Large-model FP16 conversion should react to EncodeError, not predict protobuf size
findings.observation: On winml-cli b7a7b893 with the merged PR #1176 converter, usyd-community/vitpose-plus-huge@9f36d7aec1800d23e97f10c2e74393aee92aa53f first attempted normal FP16 conversion, caught only google.protobuf.message.EncodeError from shape-inference serialization, and retried with disable_shape_infer=True. The repaired PR #1099 fp16 artifact retained float32 boundary I/O, contained 951 FLOAT16 and 0 FLOAT initializers with exactly two Cast nodes, and used 1,802,615,296 external-data bytes versus fp32's 3,605,484,544 bytes (ratio 0.4999648). This falsifies vitpose-001's ByteSize/90%-threshold fix while preserving its root-cause observation.

not_yet_tested_on: other model families whose normal FP16 conversion raises EncodeError

gotchas: Do not restore a pre-emptive ModelProto.ByteSize or approximate 2 GB threshold; attempt normal conversion and narrow the fallback to EncodeError.
A successful build or fp16 label is insufficient proof: verify initializer dtypes, expected boundary Casts, and approximately half-size external data.
findings.mechanism_notes: Git history identifies PR #1176 commit faffbe2b as the current retry implementation. The exact Huge checkpoint exercised that path, and the tester artifact audit independently verified dtype, topology, and size evidence.

findings.title: Auto-config derives normalized image ranges from processor metadata without a VitPose branch
findings.observation: The repaired PR #1099 candidate on winml-cli b7a7b893 loads the full image-processor config once and, for floating image-shaped inputs only, derives low-inclusive/high-exclusive float32 bounds from do_rescale, do_normalize, rescale_factor, image_mean, and image_std. Recipe-free config for the pinned VitPose++ Huge checkpoint emitted pixel_values float32[1,3,256,192] with [-2.1179039478302,2.640000343322754), and both CPU recipes persisted the same range. Focused regressions cover per-channel extrema, scalar/broadcast metadata, float32 nextafter upper bounds, disabled/missing/incompatible metadata fallback, and exclusion of text/non-float inputs; the implementation contains no model ID, organization, or vitpose branch.

validated_on: usyd-community/vitpose-plus-huge@9f36d7aec1800d23e97f10c2e74393aee92aa53f @ recipe-free config and CPU fp32/fp16 @ winml-cli b7a7b893 repaired candidate
generic ResNet and scalar processor-metadata unit fixtures @ repaired candidate
not_yet_tested_on: processors with nonstandard raw pixel domains other than [0,255]

gotchas: Processor metadata must explicitly enable both rescaling and normalization; otherwise preserve the existing generated range.
Apply normalized bounds only to floating image-shaped inputs, never every float tensor in a multimodal model.
The high endpoint is np.nextafter(max_valid_float32,+inf) because recipe ranges are high-exclusive.
findings.mechanism_notes: Recipe-free config acceptance, persisted build configs, semantic processor inputs, and focused generic fixtures all agree on the same metadata-driven rule. This closes vitpose-010's auto-config gap rather than duplicating its manual range derivation.

findings.title: VitPose++ Huge L3 is data-blocked, not evaluator- or model-blocked
findings.observation: Exact CPU fp32 and fp16 winml eval attempts resolved keypoint-detection, the COCO-17 schema, model loading, image/objects/keypoints/bbox/area columns, xywh boxes, and validation split, then stopped because ~/.cache/winml/datasets/coco_keypoints_val2017 contained no data files. Unlike the 52-output SynthPose case in vitpose-008, this checkpoint emits the evaluator's expected 17 COCO heatmaps; the blocker is provisioning the pinned annotation dataset, not incompatible keypoint semantics. L0 through L2 passed for both precisions before L3 was recorded as DATASET_BLOCKER.

validated_on: usyd-community/vitpose-plus-huge@9f36d7aec1800d23e97f10c2e74393aee92aa53f @ fp32/fp16 winml eval @ CPUExecutionProvider @ winml-cli b7a7b893 repaired candidate

Diligence audit: prior VitPose knowledge and recent VitPose PR history were re-read; explicit task/model-class recipe-free config passed; both exact eval attempts reached dataset loading; EP-option, export-range, and special-token harness retries are inapplicable to a missing annotation corpus; the custom L2 harness proves inference but cannot substitute for dataset-scale ground truth.
feature_gaps_filed: Evaluation unblocker: provision and pin the expected local COCO keypoints val2017 dataset/revision/split at the configured cache path, then rerun both precision tuples; no issue or PR was filed by this learner run.
findings.mechanism_notes: Both eval logs fail at the same datasets load_dataset boundary after task/schema/model resolution. The 17-output architecture matches the default COCO metric contract, isolating missing data as the blocker.
